skim: A magnitude-7.4 earthquake's death toll in western Colombia climbed to 188, with Cali and Pereira hit hardest and 1,677 injured.
A total solar eclipse swept across Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain — Europe's first since 1999 — with a deep partial eclipse visible over the UK.
US forces fired Hellfire missiles at a cargo ship's steering gear after it tried to breach Washington's blockade near Iran, as Tehran vows Hormuz stays shut until the war ends.
A Damascus court sentenced Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for crimes against humanity, including the killing of children under 15.
Intel closed an upsized $20 billion stock sale and raised its 2026 capex forecast to $20 billion to fund its AI chip and foundry buildout.

stories.headline: Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Climbs to 188
stories.body: The death toll from Monday’s magnitude-7.4 earthquake in western Colombia has climbed to 188, with 1,677 injured, per Xinhua (Aug 12). Cali was hit hardest with 95 deaths and 997 injuries, followed by Pereira with 79 deaths and 278 injuries, as rescue crews continue combing collapsed buildings. The Colombian Association of Capital Cities has launched a system to report and search for missing persons as damage assessment work continues.

stories.headline: Philippines Flood Death Toll Rises to 19, 2.27 Million Affected
stories.body: The death toll from a week of monsoon rains and Typhoon Dolphin’s outer bands in the Philippines has risen to 19, with four still missing and 2.27 million people affected across 646,676 families, per Manila Times (Aug 11), citing the NDRRMC. Benguet province has borne the brunt with 12 deaths, mostly from landslides, while Rizal and Batangas reported four and three deaths respectively. Nearly 95,000 people remain in 919 evacuation centers as infrastructure damage is estimated at ₱1.456 billion.

stories.headline: Typhoon Dolphin Floods Central China, Puts Beijing on Alert
stories.body: Typhoon Dolphin’s remnants have flooded central China and put Beijing on alert, with the capital forecast to receive more than a third of its annual rainfall within 24 hours, per Anews (Aug 11). In Hubei province, reservoir overflow forced the relocation of 9,705 people from Xiangyang, while Henan faces up to 350mm of rain through Wednesday afternoon. “This area always gets flooded when it rains. If it continues like this, the waters could reach my home,” said one 60-year-old resident of an affected district.

stories.headline: Total Solar Eclipse Sweeps Across Europe's Arctic Fringe
stories.body: A total solar eclipse sweeps across Greenland, Iceland, northern Spain and the Balearic Islands today — Europe’s first total eclipse since 1999, per Space.com (Aug 11). The moon will fully block the sun along the path of totality, plunging observers into brief twilight and revealing the solar corona, with a partial eclipse visible across much of Europe and parts of the northeastern US and eastern Canada. Skywatchers are advised to “pack your eclipse glasses, charge your camera and phone, check the latest weather forecast… arrive early if you’re traveling.”

stories.headline: Rodri-Barcelona deal reaches final stage as €55m fee agreed
stories.body: Barcelona and Manchester City have agreed a fee of around €55m plus add-ons for Rodri, with the move described by Mundo Deportivo as being in its “final stage” pending minor paperwork. Barcelona had been pushing to complete the deal so the Spain midfielder could rejoin his future teammates in Catalonia this Wednesday, straight off his post-World Cup break, per Yahoo Sports/Barca Blaugranes (Aug 10) — the arrival date flagged in yesterday's reports.

stories.headline: Liverpool complete Araujo loan from Barcelona amid defensive crisis
stories.body: Liverpool have signed Uruguay centre-back Ronald Araujo on a season-long loan from Barcelona with a £47.14m (€55m) option to buy, with no loan fee and Liverpool covering his full wages after he took a pay cut to push the move through. The signing addresses an injury crunch at Anfield — Joe Gomez is out for the Newcastle opener and new arrival Jeremy Jacquet's fitness is uncertain — with Araujo saying, “It was the ideal move for me at this stage in my career,” per Sky Sports (Aug 11).

stories.headline: Trent Rockets secure direct final berth in The Hundred, skip eliminator
stories.body: Trent Rockets have wrapped up top spot in both the men's and women's Hundred tables on 24 and 28 points respectively, meaning the men's side goes straight to Sunday's final at Lord's without having to survive Friday's eliminator against the second- and third-placed teams. The men's group stage concludes Wednesday, with eliminators on Friday (reserve Saturday) and finals on Sunday, August 16, per Sky Sports (Aug 11) — updating yesterday's note that the Rockets were fighting to avoid the eliminator.

stories.headline: Bumrah ruled out of Sri Lanka Tests, uncapped Nabi handed maiden call-up
stories.body: Jasprit Bumrah has been officially ruled out of India's two-Test tour of Sri Lanka because of the left knee injury that has troubled him since England's ODI series, with uncapped Jammu & Kashmir seamer Auqib Nabi drafted in after taking 104 wickets across his last two Ranji Trophy seasons, including 60 in the 2025-26 title-winning campaign. Sai Sudharsan was also ruled out through injury and Sarfaraz Khan has been recalled, with the squad departing for Galle ahead of the series opener on August 15, per ESPN Cricinfo.

stories.headline: Red Bull sets development plan as winless run drags on
stories.body: Red Bull technical director Pierre Waché says the team — currently fourth-fastest and still without a win 11 rounds into the 2026 season — has “a development plan until the end of the year” to fix the RB22's narrow operating window, balance problems and excess weight, adding, “Going for wins this year is what we aim for.” Max Verstappen's best result remains second at the Hungarian Grand Prix, leaving him on course for his first winless season since his 2015 rookie year at Toro Rosso, per RacingNews365 (Aug 11).

stories.headline: Wall Street Braces for July CPI Report Due Today
stories.body: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the July CPI report at 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday, with economists forecasting headline inflation of +0.1% month-over-month (+3.4% year-over-year) and core CPI of +0.32% month-over-month (+2.5% year-over-year), per Kiplinger (Aug 10). E*TRADE's Chris Larkin said “The S&P 500's breakout from a nearly two-month trading range could get a test this week from inflation and geopolitics,” with traders watching whether the data clears the path for further Fed rate cuts.

stories.headline: Brent Crude Nears $90 as Hormuz Strait Standoff Drags On
stories.body: Brent crude jumped more than 2% overnight to $89.61 a barrel as of 03:00 GMT, up roughly 24% since the US-Israel war on Iran began, per Al Jazeera (Aug 12). Only 10 vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday versus roughly 130 daily transits before the conflict; KCM Trade's Tim Waterer said “Markets have not completely lost hope for a deal, but confidence is clearly eroding.”

stories.headline: Gold Tests $4,500 Ahead of Key US Inflation Data
stories.body: Gold has climbed nearly 10% this month and is testing the psychologically key $4,500 level, with traders eyeing $5,000 next, per VT Markets (Aug 11). The report notes that hotter-than-expected July CPI data due Wednesday “could force the Fed to pause rate cuts and drag gold down,” while a soft reading would likely clear the path higher; gold opened Tuesday at $4,446.90 an ounce.

stories.headline: Cisco Set to Report Record Revenue in Q4 Results After the Bell
stories.body: Cisco Systems reports fiscal fourth-quarter earnings after Wednesday's close, with analysts expecting revenue of $16.82 billion (up from $14.67 billion a year earlier) and EPS of $1.17, which would mark a company revenue record on strong AI-infrastructure demand, per Benzinga (Aug 11). Cisco shares are up sharply year-to-date, and Freedom Capital Markets' Jay Woods said “If it can breakout, expect a new leg to accelerate higher over the coming months.”

stories.headline: Nvidia's $500 Billion Financing Coalition Eases Wall Street's Credit Jitters
stories.body: Credit-default protection on Nvidia's debt fell to roughly $73,000 per $10 million of exposure, down from a late-July peak of $82,000, after the chipmaker lined up a six-firm coalition — BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Apollo Global, Blackstone, Brookfield and KKR — to raise $500 billion for AI data centers and chip infrastructure, per Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance (Aug 11). “[This] is a positive development to take out some of the uncertainty about both infrastructure build-out and customers' future spending,” said Brett Kozlowski of GW&K Investment Management, as Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to 25% of project value, including its reported $250 billion commitment to OpenAI's Ohio data center.

stories.headline: Intel Upsizes Share Sale to $20 Billion, Lifts 2026 Capex Forecast
stories.body: Intel raised $20 billion in an expanded stock offering priced at $95 a share — up from the $15 billion first floated a day earlier — and lifted its 2026 capital-expenditure forecast to $20 billion from $18 billion, including a €5 billion ($5.77 billion) push into Irish chipmaking, per Reuters/Yahoo Finance (Aug 11). “As a capital-intensive business… it makes perfect sense for Intel to raise money,” said Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, after a rally that has nearly tripled Intel's share price this year.

stories.headline: TSMC and Sony Seal $6.3B Chip-Sensor Venture as Taiwan Stocks Hit Record
stories.body: TSMC and Sony formally signed a cooperation agreement to launch “Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing,” a roughly ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) joint venture in Japan — Sony holding 60%, TSMC 40% — targeting automotive, robotics and AR image sensors, with mass production slated for 2029, per BigGo Finance (Aug 12). The deal follows TSMC's record July revenue of NT$467.58 billion, and Taiwan's benchmark index closed above 45,000 points for the first time even as foreign investors held net-short futures positions above 88,000 contracts, signaling lingering caution.

stories.headline: Honor Launches World's First 'Robot Phone' With Robotic Camera Gimbal
stories.body: Honor officially unveiled its Robot Phone in China on August 12, built around a four-degree-of-freedom titanium-alloy robotic gimbal atop a 200MP main camera that enables “360-degree subject tracking and AI-powered cinematic camera movements,” per GSMArena and TechNode. The device runs a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset with a 6,000mAh battery and 120W charging, and includes an ARRI partnership for Log-C video recording; Honor CEO Li Jian had previewed it at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference ahead of the global rollout.

stories.headline: US disables cargo ship as Iran hardens Hormuz blockade terms
stories.body: US forces fired two Hellfire missiles at the steering mechanism of a Panama-flagged cargo vessel after it ignored warnings and tried to breach Washington's blockade near Iranian ports, per Al Jazeera (Aug 12). Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said the Strait of Hormuz stays shut until there is a “complete end to the US war and blockade, the release of its frozen assets, and a regional ceasefire,” while Qatar reported that separate Oman-Iran shipping negotiations are progressing significantly.

stories.headline: Assad and brother sentenced to death in absentia over crimes against humanity
stories.body: A Damascus criminal court sentenced ousted president Bashar al-Assad, his brother Maher al-Assad (both in absentia, exiled in Russia) and former security chief Atef Najib to death on charges including premeditated murder, torture and the killing of children under 15, per Al Jazeera (Aug 11). The judge said witness testimony established Assad as “the highest decision-maker” who “used state institutions to facilitate” the crimes, and residents of Idlib, launch point of the offensive that ended the family's 53-year rule, celebrated the verdict on Aug 12.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy says Russia used North Korean missiles in deadly Zaporizhzhia strike
stories.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said “the city was struck with North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons, and guided aerial bombs” in an overnight attack that killed six and wounded 19 in Zaporizhzhia, with three more killed in Dnipropetrovsk, per Euronews (Aug 11). He warned Russia is preparing to deploy 30,000-50,000 additional North Korean troops and is receiving more Pyongyang-made missiles, saying “this is the first time they cannot wage war without supplements from North Korea.”

stories.headline: Sudan's al-Burhan pushes national dialogue as critics call it cosmetic
stories.body: Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan held private consultations with political blocs, Sufi leaders and civil society groups to advance a national dialogue conference, reaching agreement to drop death-penalty charges against opposition leaders and form a preparatory committee, per Al Jazeera (Aug 10). But Babiker Faisal of the Somoud alliance dismissed it as a “cosmetic political process” meant to entrench army authority, while former minister Hamid Mumtaz warned any partial dialogue “would remain isolated and be doomed to fail.”

fixtures.headline: India's first Test vs Sri Lanka begins in Galle
fixtures.body: Shubman Gill leads a Bumrah-less India into the series opener at Galle International Stadium, the first of a two-match Test series.

fixtures.headline: The Hundred finals day at Lord's
fixtures.body: Trent Rockets, already through as men's group-stage winners, face the eliminator winner in Sunday's men's final, with the women's final also at Lord's the same day; eliminators are Friday at The Kia Oval.

fixtures.headline: F1 returns from summer break at the Dutch Grand Prix
fixtures.body: The paddock reconvenes at Circuit Zandvoort for the first race back from the summer shutdown, with Red Bull's development updates and Verstappen's title/future situation in focus.

fixtures.headline: Premier League 2026-27 season kicks off
fixtures.body: The new Premier League campaign begins across the weekend of August 22, a week later than usual to give players recovery time after the World Cup; newly bolstered sides like Liverpool (with loan signing Araujo) will be under early scrutiny.

portfolio.headline: Alphabet heads into tonight's Pixel 11 launch while defending a bigger AI capex bill
portfolio.body: Alphabet unveils the Pixel 11 line at an event in New York this evening, even as it defends a raised 2026 capital-expenditure outlook of $195-205 billion, up from its prior $180-190 billion range, aimed largely at AI and Cloud infrastructure. The launch follows a leadership reshuffle at DeepMind, in which Demis Hassabis moved from chief executive to chair and chief scientist while Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat departed to launch an independent AI research venture, Discovery Loop. Investors have focused less on the new hardware than on whether the increased spending will translate into durable Cloud revenue growth, per ts2.tech (Aug 11).

portfolio.headline: Amazon's AWS backlog swells to $496 billion as capex guidance rises to $220 billion
portfolio.body: AWS revenue grew 37% to $42.2 billion last quarter, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, while Amazon's total revenue climbed 20% to $200.6 billion and operating income rose 43% to $27.5 billion, per its Q2 report (MLQ, Jul 30). CEO Andy Jassy raised the company's full-year capex forecast to $220 billion from $200 billion, citing higher memory-chip costs, and said AWS's contracted backlog reached $496 billion after adding $132 billion in new bookings, warning capacity “will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026… and I believe this dynamic will also be true in 2027.”

portfolio.headline: Oracle's AI buildout is burning cash as it lines up a $40 billion capital raise
portfolio.body: Oracle's fiscal 2026 capital expenditure reached $55.7 billion against $67.4 billion in total revenue, leaving free cash flow negative by $23.7 billion even as remaining performance obligations swelled to $638 billion and customers advanced $75 billion in AI-related prepayments. The company has guided fiscal 2027 capex as high as $95 billion and plans to raise roughly $40 billion in debt and equity to fund the buildout, per CryptoBriefing (Aug 1). Analysts remain split: UBS trimmed its price target on Oracle while keeping a Buy rating on Aug 6, while BNP Paribas argued Oracle's cost-plus contract structure should preserve margins as the spending cycle peaks, per Benzinga (Aug 11).

portfolio.headline: Rackspace's cloud turnaround stalls as Q2 losses widen
portfolio.body: Rackspace Technology reported second-quarter revenue of $670 million, up about 0.6% year-over-year, with its public cloud segment declining 2.3% even as private cloud grew 5.5%. The company posted a net loss of $68 million, wider than the $55 million loss a year earlier, with operating losses also deepening to $33 million from $25 million, per GuruFocus (Aug 10). Non-GAAP operating profit held roughly flat at $27 million, underscoring the pressure the smaller cloud-infrastructure player faces competing against larger hyperscalers.

portfolio.headline: Fastly extends its rally after a Q2 beat and raised full-year guidance
portfolio.body: Fastly reported second-quarter revenue of $183.3 million, ahead of a roughly $174 million Street estimate, with adjusted earnings of $0.15 per share more than doubling the $0.07 consensus. The company posted a record non-GAAP gross margin of 65.8% and lifted its full-year outlook to $732-746 million in revenue and $0.50-0.54 in adjusted EPS, citing a net retention rate of 117%, per Benzinga (Aug 5). The move has tracked a broader rally across cloud and AI-infrastructure names including Oracle and Datadog in recent sessions, per 24/7 Wall St (Aug 10).

portfolio.headline: Beyond Meat sets a 1-for-30 reverse split to save its Nasdaq listing
portfolio.body: Beyond Meat will execute a 1-for-30 reverse stock split effective late on Aug 13, with split-adjusted trading beginning Aug 14, after shareholders approved a range of possible ratios at a November 2025 special meeting. The company said the move is meant to regain compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid-price rule, and will also cut authorized shares from 3 billion to 100 million, with convertible notes, warrants and equity awards adjusting proportionally. CEO Ethan Brown called it “an important step toward maintaining our Nasdaq listing and better positioning our stock for long-term investor participation,” per GlobeNewswire (Aug 11).

portfolio.headline: Analysts see faster-narrowing losses at gene-editing company Editas Medicine
portfolio.body: HC Wainwright raised its earnings estimates for Editas Medicine, improving its projected 2026 per-share loss and its 2027 per-share loss estimate, with similar upward revisions to near-term quarterly estimates. The reset followed Editas' second-quarter results and business update released Aug 5, and comes days after the company added cardiologist and geneticist Patrick Ellinor to its board on Aug 4. Analyst consensus on the gene-editing company remains a Moderate Buy, per MarketBeat (Aug 6).

portfolio.headline: No fresh news at Hydrofarm; the story remains a $16 million asset sale and debt paydown
portfolio.body: No company-specific announcement was found for Hydrofarm's session. Its most recent disclosure was Aug 3, when it completed the sale of Aurora Peat Products to Raven Holdings for $16 million, including a $5 million promissory note, with proceeds earmarked to reduce term-loan debt alongside the launch of “Project Agility” to scale a logistics-services business the company said reflects a shift toward becoming “a leaner, more focused organization.” Hydrofarm retains a commercial relationship with the divested peat unit and is due to report second-quarter results Aug 14, per GlobeNewswire (Aug 3).

stories.headline: Modi Urges Nation to Join 'Har Ghar Tiranga' Ahead of 80th Independence Day
stories.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on citizens to display the national flag at home as part of the fifth edition of the “Har Ghar Tiranga” campaign, running August 9-17 to mark India's 80th Independence Day. “Come, let us make #HarGharTiranga a celebration in every home,” Modi said, tying this year's drive to the 150th anniversary of the national song “Vande Mataram,” per WION (Aug 12).

stories.headline: Vande Mataram to Ring Out From Red Fort for First Time as India Marks 150 Years of the Song
stories.body: India's 80th Independence Day on August 15 will also mark 150 years since Bankim Chandra Chatterjee composed “Vande Mataram,” and the song will be sung from the Red Fort ramparts for the first time as PM Modi arrives for the flag-hoisting ceremony. About 2,500 NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will spell out the anthem's Hindi text on Gyanpath while an Indian Air Force Mi-17 helicopter showers flower petals, per WION (Aug 11).

stories.headline: India Rejects China's Objection to Renaming of 27 Places in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.body: India dismissed Beijing's objection after New Delhi formally listed 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh — including settlements, mountain passes and a lake — on official Survey of India maps on August 7. “Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India. This is a fact that is self-evident,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, while China's Guo Jiakun called the move “illegal, null and void,” per WION (Aug 12).

stories.headline: Kashmir on High Alert Ahead of Independence Day Amid Terror Threat Inputs
stories.body: Jammu and Kashmir security forces stepped up multilayered checkpoints and surveillance across Srinagar after intelligence warned Lashkar-e-Taiba could target security personnel, non-local workers or crowded venues before August 15. “Security is on alert and multilayered security arrangements have been made across the Kashmir Valley,” IGP Kashmir V K Birdi said, per WION (Aug 11).

stories.headline: Burnham 'Confident' He Can Block Early Release of PC Andrew Harper's Killers
stories.body: PM Andy Burnham said he is increasingly confident ministers can stop the early release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, jailed for manslaughter over the 2019 death of PC Andrew Harper, after a petition against their release passed 880,000 signatures. Justice Secretary Alex Norris will lay exemption plans before Parliament in September, part of a wider fast-tracked overhaul that Burnham says could also resolve the “long-running injustice” facing roughly 2,300 prisoners still held on abolished IPP sentences, per ITV News (Aug 11).

stories.headline: Burnham Fast-Tracks Ban on 'Subscription Traps' as Cost-of-Living Tour Continues
stories.body: Days into his nationwide cost-of-living tour, Burnham brought forward a ban on unwanted subscription rollovers and misleading “pretend price” discounts, with the government projecting savings of about £400 million a year, or roughly £170 per person, against 10 million unwanted active subscriptions nationwide. “I'm determined to pull every single lever we can to provide people with some room to breathe on the cost of living,” Burnham said; the new rules take effect by January 2027, per IBTimes UK (Aug 10).

stories.headline: UK Braces for Rare Deep Partial Solar Eclipse This Evening
stories.body: Skywatchers across Britain are preparing for a partial solar eclipse this evening, part of the same event bringing totality to Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain, with the Moon covering up to 96% of the Sun over Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly and around 88-91% over Scotland. The eclipse begins near 6:00-6:20pm BST and peaks between 7:00-7:17pm, with the Sun sitting only 10-16 degrees above the western horizon, per Star Walk (Aug 10).

stories.headline: Saudi and Turkish Foreign Ministers Discuss Gulf and Red Sea Security
stories.body: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan held a phone call focused on “diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions, ensure the security and freedom of navigation in the Gulf and Red Sea, and promote regional stability.” The two ministers also discussed opportunities to expand bilateral cooperation between Riyadh and Ankara, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 12).

stories.headline: Qatar's Economy Grew 2.9% in 2025 as Inflation Stayed Contained, Central Bank Says
stories.body: Qatar Central Bank's annual macroeconomic review showed real GDP growth of 2.9% in 2025, led by a 4.8% expansion in the non-hydrocarbon sector, while inflation averaged just 0.5%. Tourist arrivals rose to 5.1 million from 4.9 million, the current account surplus reached QR116.2 billion (14.8% of GDP), and the Qatar Stock Exchange posted an annual gain of 1.8%, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 11).

stories.headline: Qatar and GCC Condemn Colombia's Recognition of Israeli Sovereignty Over Golan Heights
stories.body: Qatar's Foreign Ministry said Colombia's recognition of Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Syrian Golan Heights violates UN Security Council Resolution 497, calling it “occupied Arab territory” and warning that such unilateral moves are “a major obstacle to achieving peace in the region.” The GCC Secretary-General separately said the decision “violates international law,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 11).

doha_events.headline: National Museum of Qatar hosts free Object Handling Session today
doha_events.body: NMoQ's monthly hands-on archaeology workshop returns to the museum lobby today, August 12, from 3-4:30pm, letting visitors examine stone tools and pottery sherds up close and quiz experts on how they were made and used, per Qatar Living (Aug 9). Admission is free and no registration is required.

doha_events.headline: ColorVerse Experience brings immersive family adventure to Katara
doha_events.body: An interactive, multi-zone attraction has taken over Katara Cultural Village's South Parking through September 15, where visitors become “Restorers” using projection mapping, dynamic lighting and motion-based challenges to revive the fictional world of Colorama, per The Peninsula Qatar (Jul 20). It's open to children aged 4 and up, running 4pm-10pm on weekdays and until 11pm on weekends, with tickets available via Platinumlist.

doha_events.headline: 'The Astrolabe: Taker of the Stars' exhibition runs at MIA Library through August
doha_events.body: Qatari designer Khawla Al-Essa's graphic-design display exploring the astrolabe's historic role in astronomy and navigation continues at the Museum of Islamic Art Library until August 31, featuring publications, printmaking, sketches and laser-cut models, per Qatar Living (Aug 9). Entry is free for residents and under-16s, with a QAR 50 fee for non-resident adults; the library is open daily except Wednesdays.

doha_events.headline: Bollywood Fever with DJ Raya hits Saraya Corniche Hotel Thursday
doha_events.body: The Penthouse at Saraya Corniche Hotel hosts a Bollywood-themed night on August 13 from 9pm, with DJ Raya spinning commercial Hindi and Punjabi hits, per Qatar Living's weekly events roundup (Aug 9). Entry is QAR 50.
